packageRules.description: VanillaBP artifacts, the Business Cockpit among them, follow the framework, not Renovate: their versions are bumped when a release is cut, and while they are snapshots there is nothing to look up. Without this rule every module of this repository is looked up in Maven Central as the parent of another module, and the Dependency Dashboard lists each of them as a failed lookup.
mongodb-changesets is a snapshot from the snapshot repository of Maven Central. While it is a snapshot there is no release to look up. The version is raised by hand when a release is cut.

protoc writes the classes of bpms-protobuf-api, and a generated class refuses to load on a protobuf-java older than the protoc which wrote it. Those classes run in other applications, on the protobuf-java their platform manages. So protoc stays at or below the oldest protobuf-java a supported platform manages, and it moves by hand when that platform moves. The POM of apis/bpms-api/protobuf says how. Renovate reads neither 'version.protoc' nor 'protobuf.lowest-platform-runtime' today, because no dependency names them; this rule keeps it so if protoc ever becomes a dependency of the build. protobuf-java itself, 'version.protobuf', is raised as usual: a runtime newer than the generated classes is fine.
